dhpak2.5:1.1: 2.5 The Story about the Elder Mahā Kassapa
dhpak2.5:2.1: “When the wise one eliminates heedlessness,” {1.258} this Dhamma teaching was given by
dhpak2.5:2.2: the Teacher while he was in residence at Jetavana with reference to the Elder Mahā Kassapa.
dhpak2.5:3.1: For on a certain day, while the elder was in residence at Pipphali Cave, he made his round of Rājagaha for alms,
dhpak2.5:3.2: and after he had returned from his rounds for alms and had eaten his breakfast, he increased the light
dhpak2.5:3.3: and sat down, surveying with his divine eye beings, both heedless and heedful,
dhpak2.5:3.4: passing away and coming into existence in the water, on the earth, on the mountains, and elsewhere.
dhpak2.5:4.1: The Teacher, seated at Jetavana, {1.259} exercised the divine eye and
dhpak2.5:4.2: pondered within himself: “With what is my son Kassapa occupied today?”
dhpak2.5:4.3: Straightaway he became aware of the following: “He is contemplating the passing away and coming into existence of living beings.”
dhpak2.5:4.4: And he said: “The passing away and coming into existence of living beings cannot be fully reckoned even by a Buddha’s knowledge.
dhpak2.5:4.5: It is impossible to reckon the beings who, having obtained conception
dhpak2.5:4.6: in a mother’s womb, pass away without their mother or father knowing.
dhpak2.5:4.7: To know them is beyond your range, Kassapa, for your range is very slight.
dhpak2.5:4.8: It comes within the [28.312] range of the Buddhas alone to know and to see in
dhpak2.5:4.9: their totality the passing away and coming into existence of living beings.”
dhpak2.5:4.10: So saying, he sent forth a radiance, and as it were sitting down face to face with Kassapa, pronounced the following verse:
dhpak2.5:5.1: When the wise one eliminates heedlessness with his heedfulness, and mounts the palace of wisdom,
dhpak2.5:5.2: griefless, he looks on grieving people;
dhpak2.5:5.3: the wise one, like one standing on a mountain, looks down on the fools, who are standing on the plains.
dhpak2.5:7.1: At the conclusion of the verse many realised the fruition of Stream-entry and so on.
